road.name: Forest Road 38 (via Mosquito Lake Road from Acme) to the Elbow Lake Trail's north trailhead (a separate trailhead from Pioneer Camp, which is on the trail's south end via Baker Lake Highway/FSR 12)
road.status: Damaged by December 2025 flooding; no Forest Service repair timeline published as of mid-2026 — confirm current status with the Mount Baker Ranger District before driving in.
road.driveNote: From the Mount Baker Ranger District (Sedro-Woolley), take WA-9 north to Acme, turn right on Mosquito Lake Road for ~9 miles, cross the Middle Fork Nooksack River, then continue on FSR 38 for ~11 miles to the trailhead.
road.seasonalGate: Normally gated at Wallace Creek (~1.3 miles before the trailhead) roughly December 1 through June 15, independent of flood damage.

access.fees: $5 daily or $30 annual Northwest Forest Pass.
access.rules: Standard Forest Service dispersed-use/Leave No Trace rules apply for day use and backcountry camping.
access.permit: No day-use climbing permit required; standard Mount Baker Wilderness group-size/LNT rules apply.
access.closures: FSR 38, the primary access road, was significantly damaged in the December 2025 floods; as of mid-2026 the Forest Service (per District Ranger Louis Neff) has no published repair timeline for it. The unofficial log crossing with rope handrails over the Middle Fork Nooksack at the Elbow Lake trailhead was also destroyed in the same storms and has not been replaced. Even in a normal year, FSR 38 has a seasonal gate at Wallace Creek, about 1.3 miles before the trailhead, closed roughly December 1 through June 15.
access.landManager: U.S. Forest Service — Mount Baker Ranger District, Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Sedro-Woolley, WA).
access.land_manager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mount Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness
access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
access.passRequired: Northwest Forest Pass (or an America the Beautiful / National Parks pass) displayed at the Elbow Lake Trail's north trailhead (FSR 38) — a separate trailhead from Pioneer Camp, which is on the trail's south end via Baker Lake Highway/FSR 12.

overnight_permit.where: Camping is on unregulated Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest land; no wilderness permit or registration is needed.

approach: From the Mount Baker Ranger District office in Sedro-Woolley, drive north on WA-9 to Acme, turn right (east) on Mosquito Lake Road for about 9 miles, cross the Middle Fork Nooksack River, and continue onto Forest Road 38 for roughly 11 miles to the Elbow Lake Trail's north trailhead (a separate trailhead from 'Pioneer Camp,' which is actually on the trail's south end via Baker Lake Highway/FSR 12). From there, follow Elbow Lake Trail #697 across the Middle Fork Nooksack and up to a switchback near Hildebrand Creek, then pick up the unmaintained Green Creek climbers' path into the Green Creek Cirque beneath Skookum's north/east flank before gaining the ridge. As of mid-2026 this whole approach is compromised: FSR 38 was damaged in the December 2025 floods with no published repair date, and the unofficial log crossing with rope handrails over the Middle Fork Nooksack near the trailhead was also washed out — confirm current conditions with the Mount Baker Ranger District before driving in.

road.name: Twin Sisters / DNR logging roads
road.status: Network of gravel logging roads, gated in places; the FR 38 corridor used to reach this approach sustained washout damage in the December 2025 Whatcom County floods and, as of mid-2026, has no announced repair timeline — treat as foot/bike access only until confirmed otherwise.
road.driveNote: Verify current access; gates can add foot mileage

access.fees: No trailhead fee; the private timberland road beyond the gate requires the landowner's fee recreation access permit
access.rules: Respect private land and gate closures; Leave No Trace
access.permit: Check current access; some roads gated or restricted
access.closures: Logging road gates vary; access can be restricted, and the Middle Fork Nooksack Road (FR 38) sustained washout damage in the December 2025 floods with no announced repair timeline as of mid-2026.
access.landManager: Washington DNR / private timber lands (Olivine Corp.) on the lower logging-road approach, transitioning to Mount Baker Wilderness (Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Mt. Baker Ranger District) on the upper mountain -- matches the sibling West Ridge route.
access.land_manager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness
access.parking_pass: No developed fee trailhead here — FR 38 gate/pullout is an undeveloped roadside parking spot; no Northwest Forest Pass required.

overnight_permit.where: Camping is on unregulated Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest land (camping is not allowed on the private timberland below it); no wilderness permit or registration is needed. The Dailey Prairie logging-road gate is separately locked to vehicles by the timber company, which is an access issue unrelated to camping.

road.name: FR 38 (Middle Fork Road) via Mosquito Lake Road off WA-542
road.status: Gravel Forest Service road, rougher toward its end; FR 38 sustained washout damage in the December 2025 Whatcom County floods and, as of mid-2026, has no announced repair timeline — vehicle access beyond the damage point is not advised (foot/bike travel only). Confirm current drivable distance with the Mt. Baker Ranger District before your trip.
road.driveNote: From WA-542 just past milepost 16, take Mosquito Lake Road ~4.8 miles, then FR 38 south to the Middle Fork Nooksack River bridge/gate area, where the old logging/quarry-road approach to the Twin Sisters basin begins.

approach: The X Couloir is approached from the south via the Middle Fork Nooksack River Road (FR-38), not from Heliotrope Ridge (that trailhead serves Lincoln's separate NW Face/Wilkes-Booth line). Drive FR-38 toward its mile-12.5 switchback and start hiking/bushwhacking the old decommissioned road around Pt. 4481 toward Rankin Creek — snow travel (often by bike or snowshoe on the lower stretch) leads past East Rankin Lake (~5,120 ft) and up into the basin to a sheltered camp at treeline around 6,100 ft, near the highest trees in the basin below Seward Peak. From camp, an alpine start gets the team into the southwest basin and across the bergschrund crux while it's still cold and firm, climbing roughly 1,500 ft of 30-40° snow and a steep serac step in the X Couloir to the 9,085 ft summit. Total approach is on the order of 7 miles and 3,350 ft of gain to the basin camp. IMPORTANT — access note: as of mid-2026, FR-38 (Middle Fork Nooksack River Road) is closed at milepost 7 by a washout from the December 2025 floods, with no confirmed repair timeline, and a separate seasonal gate at Wallace Creek (~mile 10) closes the road December 1-June 15 for elk calving; confirm current road status with the Mount Baker Ranger District (Glacier Public Service Center) before a trip, since the drivable road-end — and therefore the length of the approach — varies year to year.

road.name: Baker Lake Road (FR-11) to FR-1106/FR-1107, Anderson & Watson Lakes Trailhead
road.driveNote: As of July 2026, FR-1107 (Anderson-Watson Road) is closed at Mile Post 3.8 due to a washout — this blocks vehicle access to the standard Anderson & Watson Lakes Trailhead. The shorter, brushier Bacon Creek Road (FR-1060) to spur NF-1064 on the mountain's SE side (~800 ft start) has no reported closure at this time and is currently the only drivable approach; verify current road/washout status before relying on either, as conditions change.

road.name: Deadhorse Road (Forest Service Road 37)
road.status: Closed to vehicles at mile 0.03 since 1 June 2026 while flood-damage repair is under way, with no end date given, as listed on the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest alert still posted on 25 September 2026
road.driveNote: From Glacier, drive SR 542 east about 1 mile, turn right onto Glacier Creek Road (FS 39), then take an immediate left onto Deadhorse Road (FS 37); FS 37 normally continues 12.7 miles to the Skyline Divide Trailhead, but is currently gated at mile 0.03 for repair work.
road.seasonalGate: No routine seasonal gate reported for FS 37 itself; access is presently blocked by the repair closure regardless of season

approach: From Glacier, WA, drive Mt. Baker Highway (SR 542) east about 1 mile past the Glacier Public Service Center to Glacier Creek Road (FS 39); turn right, then take an immediate left onto Deadhorse Road (FS 37). FS 37 normally continues 12.7 miles to the Skyline Divide Trailhead. FS 37 is currently closed to vehicles at mile 0.03 while the 2021 flood washout at milepost 3.1 is repaired, so the trailhead is not currently reachable by vehicle. When open, hike Skyline Divide Trail #678 through old-growth forest switchbacks and into meadows on the ridge crest (~2 mi), follow the crest to the trail's high point (~6,563 ft, ~4.5 mi), then continue cross-country along the open ridge to Chowder Ridge and the base of Hadley Peak.

road.name: Hannegan Pass Road (FR-32)
road.status: Gravel Forest Service road; per the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie NF, currently has limited access for larger vehicles due to flood damage. High-clearance and/or 4WD recommended for the last few miles.
road.driveNote: SR 542 east from Glacier ~12.5 miles, then left on FR-32 for 5.3 miles to the Hannegan Trailhead (~3,100 ft).
road.seasonalGate: Typically snow-free and driveable by early-mid June; unmaintained in winter.

road.name: Hannegan Pass Road (FR-32)
road.status: Gravel Forest Service road; per the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie NF, currently has limited access for larger vehicles due to flood damage. Potholed and bumpy — high-clearance and/or 4WD recommended for the last few miles.
road.driveNote: SR 542 east from Glacier ~12.5 miles, then left on FR-32 for 5.3 miles to the Hannegan Trailhead (~3,100 ft).
road.seasonalGate: Typically snow-free and driveable by early-mid June; not plowed or maintained in winter.

road.name: Harts Pass Road (Lost River Rd -> FR 9140 -> FR 5400)
road.status: Closed to vehicles from the Monument Creek Trailhead through Harts Pass as of mid-2026 due to December 2025 storm/flood damage; USFS targeted a mid-July 2026 reopening but this should be reconfirmed before travel. Passable on foot/bike even while vehicle-closed.
road.driveNote: From Winthrop, WA drive about 15 miles west on Highway 20, turn onto Lost River Road (County Road 9140), continue on pavement then gravel FR 5400 to reach the Robinson Creek or Monument Creek trailheads. The road has a recent history of multi-month storm-damage closures beyond Monument Creek Trailhead — check current Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest alerts before driving in.
road.seasonalGate: In a normal (non-storm-damage) year the road and Harts Pass typically open to vehicles by early-mid summer (around the Fourth of July); high-elevation portions can hold snow into June.

access.fees: No wilderness entry fee; a Northwest Forest Pass is not required at the primitive Robinson Creek / Slate Pass / Monument Creek trailheads used to approach this peak (only posted developed day-use sites require it).
access.rules: Group size capped at 12 people / 18 head of stock.
access.permit: Free self-issue wilderness permit required at the trailhead register (no quota, no reservation, no cost).
access.closures: Harts Pass Road (Lost River Rd / FR 9140 -> FR 5400) has been closed to vehicles from the Monument Creek Trailhead through Harts Pass since storm/flood damage in December 2025, cutting off the Robinson Creek, Slate Pass, and Slate Peak trailheads used for the standard approaches. As of a June 17, 2026 report the road remained closed with the Forest Service targeting a mid-July 2026 reopening at the earliest; the road stays open to foot/bike traffic even when vehicle-closed. Verify current status with the Methow Valley Ranger District or PCTA's closures page before planning a trip.
access.landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District — Pasayten Wilderness
access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at trailheads (e.g. Andrews Creek, Chewuch River) — $5/day or $30/annual.

overnight_permit.where: Fill one out at the trailhead registration box. No reservation is needed.

road.name: Lost River Road / Harts Pass Road (Forest Road 5400)
road.status: Closed to vehicles beyond the Monument Trailhead (2,400 ft) since a December 2025 storm; repair timeline for the 2026 season was unconfirmed as of spring 2026 — verify current status with the Methow Valley Ranger District before the trip.
road.driveNote: From Mazama, follow Lost River Road west/north — it becomes FR-5400 — toward Harts Pass; the Monument Trailhead is reached well before the pass and is currently the effective end of vehicle access.
road.seasonalGate: In a typical (non-storm-damage) year, snow-closed roughly late October through late June/early July.

access.fees: No trailhead fee; the self-issue wilderness permit is free and a Northwest Forest Pass is not required for it.
access.rules: Pasayten Wilderness rules: campfires are prohibited above 5,000 ft elevation (well below this route, so no fires on the mountain itself); groups larger than 12 people (or 18 stock) must split into separate parties spaced at least 1 mile apart; practice Leave No Trace; no mechanized or motorized equipment.
access.permit: Free, self-issued wilderness permit required at the trailhead; non-quota, no advance reservation needed.
access.closures: Harts Pass Road (FR-5400) is currently closed to vehicle traffic beyond the Monument Trailhead due to December 2025 storm damage; it remains open to foot/bike/horse travel, and as of spring 2026 it was unclear whether it would be repaired for the summer season — check current Methow Valley Ranger District conditions before relying on the Buckskin Ridge/Slate Pass trailhead.
access.landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District (Pasayten Wilderness)
access.parking_pass: Not required — free self-issue wilderness permit only; no Northwest Forest Pass needed at this trailhead.

overnight_permit.where: Fill one out at the trailhead registration box. No reservation is needed.

road.name: North Cascades Highway (SR-20) to Ross Lake trailheads (Ross Dam Trailhead, milepost 134) or Ross Lake Resort for water-taxi access; Silver-Skagit Road (gravel, BC) serves the currently-closed Hozomeen approach.
road.status: paved on SR-20 to the trailheads; gravel on the BC-side Silver-Skagit Road
road.driveNote: SR-20 is paved and generally in good condition but closes seasonally over Washington Pass/Rainy Pass (typically mid-November through April/May depending on snowpack). Silver-Skagit Road is a rough ~39-mile gravel road from Hope, BC, but currently provides no legal access to Castle Peak because the Hozomeen border gate is closed to crossing.
road.seasonalGate: SR-20 North Cascades Highway: winter closure, typically mid-November to April/May. Silver-Skagit Road (BC): seasonal closure roughly Oct 15-Apr 14.

road.name: SR-20 (North Cascades Highway) to Ross Lake Resort; Silver Skagit Road from Hope, BC (currently closed at the border)
road.status: SR-20 is open seasonally and closes for winter avalanche danger (recent closures have run roughly early December through spring) between the Ross Dam trailhead and Silver Star Gate — check WSDOT/NPS road conditions before driving. The Silver Skagit Road remains open on the Canadian side but the border crossing into Hozomeen is closed to travelers.
road.driveNote: Drive SR-20 to Ross Lake Resort (near Diablo/Ross Dam) and arrange the resort's water taxi (206-486-3751) to shuttle you the length of Ross Lake to the Hozomeen/Lightning Creek area, or hike in via the ~31-mile East Bank Trail from the SR-20 trailhead at milepost 138.
road.seasonalGate: Hozomeen Campground on the US side is open roughly late May through October; road passability should be checked directly before a trip.

road.name: SR-20 (North Cascades Highway) to Ross Lake Resort; Silver Skagit Road from Hope, BC (currently closed at the border)
road.status: SR-20 is open seasonally and closes for winter avalanche danger (recent closures have run roughly early December through spring) between the Ross Dam trailhead and Silver Star Gate — check WSDOT/NPS road conditions before driving. The Silver Skagit Road remains open on the Canadian side but the border crossing into Hozomeen is closed to travelers.
road.driveNote: Drive SR-20 to Ross Lake Resort (near Diablo/Ross Dam) and arrange the resort's water taxi (206-486-3751) to shuttle you the length of Ross Lake to the Hozomeen/Lightning Creek area, or hike in via the ~31-mile East Bank Trail from the SR-20 trailhead at milepost 138.
road.seasonalGate: Hozomeen Campground on the US side is open roughly late May through October; road passability should be checked directly before a trip.

approach: There is no US road to Hozomeen. From the Trans-Canada Highway (BC Hwy 1) take Exit 168 at Hope, British Columbia, follow Flood-Hope Road onto Silver-Skagit Road, and drive roughly 34 miles / 55 km of gravel south through Skagit Valley Provincial Park to the Skyline II trailhead — about an hour and a quarter. Verify the border gate status first: NPS currently prohibits both vehicle and foot traffic across the boundary at Hozomeen. From Skyline II, climb the trail roughly 8 miles and 4,000 ft to the Hozomeen Ridge junction, then turn south on the Hozomeen Ridge Trail over rolling terrain to a camp near the Monument 74 high point at about 6,345 ft, 10.5 miles in. Take water from the three creeks in the forest below Hozomeen Ridge — there is no running water again until you are south of the border. From camp the climb begins by dropping about 545 ft to the 5,800 ft saddle at the head of the north cirque. A shorter but much nastier alternative starts at the Hozomeen ranger station, follows the short Trail of the Obelisk loop, then bushwhacks east up the overgrown border swath past a swamp and gains about 3,000 ft to a col near 6,300 ft before joining the ridge; it saves miles and costs hours.

A two-stage approach and the second stage is the part that stops people. Day one is a long haul of 11-plus miles under heavy loads from the road to a camp just north of the peak - the same Hozomeen Ridge / border-swath ground used by the north-side scrambling routes, reached from Silver-Skagit Road out of Hope, B.C. From that camp the approach to the base took the first ascent party a tedious and painstaking 4.5 hours: downclimb a loose third-class gully, which the party described as dangerous but the lesser of the two evils, then cross several precipitous rocky ribs and steep, unstable ground to traverse into the launch point below the wall. Budget the base approach as a half-day objective in its own right and do it in daylight. Confirm the NPS border-gate status before planning; the crossing at Hozomeen is currently closed to vehicles and foot traffic.

Same as the East Route to Lyman Lake/Cloudy Pass — via the currently-closed Lucerne/Holden Village/Railroad Creek trail from the east, or via the open Phelps Creek/Spider Gap trail from the west. From Lyman Lake or Cloudy Pass, gain the ridge crest at Cloudy Pass (6,440 ft) to start the traverse.
